chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the one in Ihram clips the nails of his hands and his feet in one place, so upon him is one blood (of a slaughtered animal); and if they were in two different places, so upon him would be two bloods (of two slaughtered animals).

key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood (a specific sacrificial penalty, usually a sheep, for breaking a ritual rule)
key_terms.مُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for clipping nails in different places while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the specific penalty (*dam*) for clipping nails while in Ihram, distinguishing between a unified act and separate acts based on location. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the precision of ritual purity laws, where the physical separation of the act determines the multiplicity of the expiation, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on intent and physical manifestation in worship.
